newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP to wind down Newcastle works - paper.
newsitem.headline: BHP to wind down Newcastle works - paper.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd is expected to reveal on Tuesday details of a far-reaching review of its steel operations which includes the virtual closure of its Newcastle works, the Sydney Morning Herald reported.
The newspaper said the winding down of the Newcastle works would be part of a plan to cut A$500 million in costs in the steel division over the next 18 months.

"The division's 12,000 workers are expected to be told the broad plans at meetings at the three major steelworks - Newcastle (New South Wales), Port Kembla (New South Wales) and Whyalla (South Australia) - tomorrow morning," it said.
It said the Australian Workers Union was expecting 3,000 jobs to disappear at the Newcastle works, which opened in 1915.

The newspaper said the plant's "front end", comprising two aging blast furnaces and coke ovens, is likely to be closed by 2000, leaving only the rod, bar and wire mills which employ about 900 workers.
"BHP is rumoured to have told major customers that it plans to be out of steel by 2020," the newspaper said.
The newspaper said the review was also likely to involve a rethink on BHP's Asian expansion strategy of recent years due to strong competitive pressures.
Company officials were not available for comment.
